expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: a plain 'are you sure?' modal won't fix this

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: people click through confirm dialogs on reflex the moment they see them often enough

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: What actually fixes...is making the action reversible instead of gating it

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: recommends dialog naming the object but not explicitly type-the-name pattern

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: make it name the actual object ('Delete Acme Corp workspace — 4 seats, 1,204 files?')

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: lists three numbered options but does not explicitly rank them as preferences
